newsitem.title: NORWAY: Christiania, Storebrand eye Nordic market.
newsitem.headline: Christiania, Storebrand eye Nordic market.

text.p: Norway's Storebrand ASA and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA said on Wednesday their merged company may be looking to expand in the Nordic financial market.
But they said they had no concrete plans for the moment, either on an all-Nordic basis or at home.
"The most important competitors in our home market are our Nordic competitors," said Aage Korsvold, chief executive officer at Storebrand, Norway's biggest insurer.
"It does not mean we are going to start a big wave of acquisitions outside Norway. But it may be that we should intensify our efforts in the other Nordic countries," he told a news conference.
Korsvold, who is proposed to be CEO of the new Christiania, said he hoped the merger with the country's second biggest bank would be completed by year-end conditional of approval by the government.
Borger Lenth, chief executive officer at Christiania Bank, said the joint company would have no immediate plans to expand further in Norway's crowded financial community.
"This is a business in movement, a market in movement," he said. "Nobody can say what will happen and what should be done next. But there are no concrete plans on what the next step will be."
